Question: Why does lying, deception & exploitaiton generally get you further in life than honesty & truth, when it comes to financial & social success?
Answer: It is easy to speak the truth because speaking the truth does not require intelligence or even deliberate thinking. Even a machine like a computer always speaks the truth only. Lying, on the other hand, requires intelligence because a lie is spoken to achieve a purpose, which involves the manipulation of the thoughts of other people. The most difficult part of a lie is that the listener must consider the words of the speaker as true, else a lie would have no impact on them, and you won't be able to achieve your purpose. Consider the following Aesops’s Fable about the two travellers. Two men were travelling together in a jungle. One traveller had never spoken a lie. The other traveller had never spoken a truth in his life. Soon they reached the land of Apes. The King of Apes ordered them to be brought to the court. To impress them, he sat on a magnificent golden throne and his subjects sat on either side. The King of Apes asked the traveller who never spoke the truth, ‘What do you think of me as a King?’ The lying traveller said, ‘Sir, everyone can see that you are the noblest and mightiest King in the whole world.’ The King was quite pleased and continued, ‘And what do you think of my subjects? ‘Sir, your subjects are all worthy of their great royal master’, said the lying traveller. The King was delighted with this answer and rewarded him handsomely. Now the King of Apes asked the honest traveller, ‘And what, Sir, is your opinion?’ The honest traveller replied, ‘I think you are simply a very fine ape, and all your subjects are fine apes, too.’ The King of Apes got very angry. He ordered him to be put to death. [1] You can see from the story that the lying traveller was smart while speaking a lie. He did not say anything false, but at the same time, he was able to make the king of apes happy and win the rewards. The honest traveller, on the other side, did not think what the king wished to hear and spoke what he thought to be true. This angered the king and he had to lose his life. Most people consider lying, heating or deception as always evil. The fact is that sometimes you have to lie and cheat to defeat a bigger evil. You must heard the story of a lion and hare, who by lying and cheating the lion, could get rid of the lion and save the lives of numerous fellow animals. [2] There is no truth in the statement that liers and cheats succeed more than honest people. The liars take risk by lying because if their lies are caught, their reputation is gone forever and they have to go to jail and live ignominious lives. Millions of liars and cheats are languishing in jail because their acts were caught. Many of them would die in prison and would never get to set foot on the free world. A small number of cheats and frauds, who are smart enough to commit the crime and not caught achieve great success in life, till they are caught. However, once they are caught, they lose everything they have acquired in life and are back to square one. We all know numerous top politicians, saints and business leaders who were billionaires once, but today they have lost everything and some of them are in prison for years. Yet there are some cheats, who become so big by cheating consciously without being caught that they seem to rule the world. However, these people are exceptions, who don’t prove the rule. The successful cheats and frauds are like the winners of a billion-dollar lottery by chance, and we must always consider the millions who too bought the lottery and lost their money. Most people become successful billionaires, not by cheating or by buying lottery tickets, but because of their hard work and innovation. An honest person may not rise to the exceptional height of the cheats who got lucky repeatedly, but he also never goes to prison or loses his reputation. On the average, an honest person achieves far more success than cheaters, most of whom usually ends up behind a bar or face ignominy, although a few of them may achieve great success in life. It is one thing to be honest, but another thing to be foolish. Only when you are honest as well as intelligent, you can achieve great success in life. So, if you fail in life, don’t blame honesty for it, but instead focus on sharpening your intelligence by acquiring more knowledge and skills to perform better and produce results in your chosen profession. Question: Why is it so difficult for most people to develop the resolve to take the path less traveled?
Answer: We humans are social animals and it is scary to travel on a path where you can’t see any person travelling with you. Most people prefer to live their lives by following the herd because they feel safe with them. Hence, most people study hard during their younger days, get a job, get married, have kids, take care of their responsibilities, provide them with a good education, get them married and then spend time with their grandchildren. This conventional path is the easiest and safest. For instance, in FY 23, 8.12 million new jobs were created by Indian companies, including 2.06 million jobs in IT sector alone. [1] So, if you have followed the common path by doing engineering, particularly in computer science and IT, and you stand even at the 2 millions position in India, you can hope to get a job and earn a decent living. Now, think about the people who are following the path less travelled, and choose to become writers, actors, artists, musicians, singers, cricketers or other sportspersons etc. The possibilities of success and earning a decent income in the less-travelled path is very small. You are practically a nobody in any creative field unless you are in the top 0.1%. For instance, In the creative field, it is the winner takes all, and if you don’t stand in the top 0.1%, you are a failure. Thus the failure rate is very high, more than 99%. The best example is Quora itself, which has over 400 million monthly active users.[3] Even if 10% of them are writers, there are at least 40 Million writers on Quora. However, hardly a few thousand writers on Quora may be getting decent views and upvotes. How disappointed do you feel when no one recognises and appreciates your work, even if its quality may be better than the so-called top writers on Quora? The same thing happens when you write a book with years of effort and can’t sell even a few hundred copies of the book to cover even the printing cost. It is true that a small percentage of people who travel on the path-less-travelled discover new territories and become world-famous, but most people get lost on this path. The following cartoon tells the story of most people who walk on the path less travelled.[4] Jerry Seinfeld said it aptly, “Sometimes the road less traveled is less traveled for a reason”. Hence, instead of choosing the road less travelled based on anecdotal evidence and emotions, find out the reasons why fewer people are travelling on a particular path. Once you understand the real reasons for people avoiding the path-less-travelled, prepare yourself well to face the challenges and pain of your new venture, and make a proper strategy to achieve success in your chosen path. Scott Peck, author of the best-selling book The Road Less Traveled, said this wisely, “Life is difficult. This is a great truth, one of the greatest truths. It is a great truth because once we truly see this truth, we transcend it. Once we truly know that life is difficult, once we truly understand and accept it, then life is no longer difficult. Because once it is accepted, the fact that life is difficult no longer matters”. Source

Question: What does it mean to have a "no regrets" attitude in life? How does it feel and what are the benefits?
Answer: If there is something which even God can’t change, it is past. Therefore, if you regret something you have done in the past, it is a useless exercise that affects your present and future. The American author L. Ron Hubbard wisely said, “Never regret yesterday. Life is in you today, and you make your tomorrow.” We often regret either the actions that have gone wrong or the right actions that we did not take at the right time. For instance, you may regret an investment that failed to yield the desired profit or a profitable investment that you did not make. We somehow feel that if we get an opportunity, we will go into the past and change our actions. However, it is impossible to go back into the past and correct the mistake. Hence, instead of wasting our time worrying, we must try to learn the lessons from our past mistakes and use that knowledge to perform the right actions in the present to create a better future for ourselves. I agree completely with Oprah Winfrey, “Failure is a great teacher and, if you are open to it, every mistake has a lesson to offer.” Abraham Lincoln can be easily considered as the person who suffered the most failures in his life. However, instead of regretting his past actions, he learned from every failure and became one of the greatest Presidents of the United States of America. I, too, have made many mistakes in the past and failed many times. However, instead of regretting, I have always learned from my mistakes and ensured that I don’t make the same mistakes again in my life. Due to my no-regret attitude, I often take big challenges in life because I know that even if I fail, I will at least learn a valuable lesson, which will improve my chances of success in the future. Question: What do you think of Narendra Modi?
Answer: I am not a great fan of Mr Narendra Modi. I don’t like many of his actions, but I also appreciate his many actions, his leadership skills, his courage to follow his conviction and take difficult decisions. He is today the most popular leader of India with a huge margin. He is so confident of his success that he even made a public announcement of his massive victory in Parliament regarding the 2024 General Election. While you can dispute the numbers, you can’t dispute him coming back to power as PM for the third time. Mr Narendra Modi reminds me the following Quote of Mahatma Gandhi, “First, they will ignore you, then they will laugh at you, then they will fight you, then you will win.” He is the undisputed winner of Indian politics today. Interestingly, Modi does not follow Gandhi’s concept of the purity of means, which in the words of Gandhi ji is, “They say 'means are after all means'. I would say 'means are after all everything'. As the means so the end... There is no wall of separation between means and end”. Instead, he strongly believes in winning at any cost and follows the words of Vince Lombardi, “Winning isn’t everything, it’s the only thing.” It is well said, “Nothing succeeds like success, and nothing exceeds like excess.” Source of picture: Google Images

Question: What is the reason behind many Indians being hesitant to ask questions? How can this fear be overcome and encourage them to ask questions?
Answer: After being selected for the IRS, my first posting was in a Central Excise Division. As a young officer, I did lots of things in the division, like renovating the office, installing computers, etc. I also booked a number of cases, some of them involved a noble modus operenti. After a couple of months, the Member Central Board of Excise and Customs (CBIC) visited the place. My Joint Commissioner (JC), who was quite fond of me and appreciated my initiative, requested the member to visit my division. Accordingly, the Member, with the Commissioner and other senior officers, made an unscheduled visit to my office and inspected my office. When the Member was having tea in my office, he casually asked me to discuss some recent cases. I had then booked an excellent case involving a huge amount of revenue and had all India ramifications. I enthusiastically started explaining the case to the member. However, the Member had little patience. He immediately told me that I had no case. He must have wondered, ‘How can a young officer with less than six months of experience make a case that they could not think of?’ However, I was prepared well and told him about the legal points, case laws, etc. The Member had no answer to my questions. He got irritated and said, “Do you want a solution or want to create a problem?” My JC was sitting next to me. He pressed my hand, signalling me to keep quiet. I submitted to the member, “I want a solution.” He then gave his reasoning about the case, and I told him that I would surely look into the case afresh. My JC later told me, “Never argue with Member. If he becomes happy, he will call you to the Board (where you get no facility), and if he gets angry, he will post you to some God-forsaken place.” I booked the case anyway, but I learned a valuable lesson: I must avoid arguing with seniors. This is how the Indian mind works. If you are a senior, older, or have a higher degree, you automatically become superior to those who are junior, younger or have lesser qualifications. India is a highly hierarchical society, and its impact is visible in every single institution. The worst thing is that you can never change your position in the hierarchy, no matter how good, competent, or hardworking you may be. Due to rigid hierarchy, you achieve your high position without merit. Hence, if someone junior questions you, he is indirectly challenging your authority, for which the person needs to be punished. Our training starts at a younger age, when we are told that we should not question our teachers because their status is even above God. Sant Kabir said this in the following Doha, "Guru Govind dou khade, kaake laagoon paye Balihari guru aapki, Govind diyo milaye." Translation I face both God and my guru. Whom should I bow to first? I first bow to my guru because he's the one who showed me the path to God.[1] We don’t question our philosophies like that of Gita or Buddha because older is always superior to younger. While humans around the world are getting smarter with time, Indians are getting so dumb that they can not even match the wisdom and knowledge acquired by their ancestors thousands of years ago. Most Indians still believe that Vedas, Upanishads and Puranas written several thousand years ago have all the wisdom of the world, including the scientific knowledge, without even reading them. India may be the only society in the world that considers its mythologies History. Even today, the entire politics revolves around mythologies, which everyone must accept as true without seeking any proof or validation. If you ask questions, you are called sickular, anti-national, anti-religion, traitor etc., and ridiculed. In such an environment, how can one ask questions? However, unless we ask questions, we can’t grow as a person, and India can’t grow as a nation. Karl Popper has wisely said, “The growth of knowledge depends entirely on disagreement”. You must overcome this fear yourself, travel on the path less travelled, and achieve success in life. Once you become successful, most Indians will make you their IDOL, follow you like a devotee, accept your wisdom as the words of God, and thus become wiser themselves.
